caption: The big red button on a toy fire engine is pressed, and its roof lights flash.

sa.check: A toy fire engine with a big red button.
The roof lights are dark before the press.
The order is dark, press, flashing.

pc.expect: The roof lights start flashing at the moment the button is pressed, and only then.
pc.fail: The button is pressed and the lights stay dark to the end of the clip; or the lights flash before the press; or the lights come on with nothing touching the engine; or a different part of the toy lights while the roof stays dark.

pc.expect: Once started, the lights flash at a steady rhythm; they stop only after a stretch or at another press and do not stop and restart on their own.
pc.fail: The flashing stops and restarts by itself; or the rhythm jumps about; or the lights settle to a steady glow and then flash again; or the flashing fades out and returns.

pc.expect: Each flash lights the roof and the surface around the engine in the lights' colour.
pc.fail: The lights flash while the roof and surface beside them stay as dark as before; or the surface glows while the lights are dark; or the glow on the surface is a different colour from the lights.

pc.expect: The engine stays where it stands apart from the hand's nudge; its ladder and doors do not move by themselves.
pc.fail: The engine lifts or slides across the floor with no hand on it; or the ladder rises by itself; or the doors open; or nearby toys jump at the press.

pc.expect: One engine with its roof lights and wheels attached; the finger passes through nothing.
pc.fail: A light or wheel vanishes or appears; or a second engine appears; or the finger passes into the toy; or the engine changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The engine's red paint and decals and the floor stay the same apart from the flashing.
pc.fail: The paint changes colour; or the decals change; or the floor pattern changes.

note: The siren is sound and is not judged.
